Subject: SOC2 Type II and interim residency confirmation for Redwood deployment in EU

Hi Logan,

We are in the middle of a vendor risk re-evaluation at NordicBank and Redwood is in scope. Two quick asks from our Security & Procurement teams:

1) Can you provide your SOC 2 Type II report covering an audit period that includes Oct 1, 2025 — Mar 31, 2026 (or an equivalent recent window)? We will accept a redacted PDF.

2) If the audit covering that window is still in progress, can Redwood provide a signed bridge letter committing to EU data residency and to not exporting customer content outside the EU for the audit window? We need the bridge letter to satisfy our evidence checklist.

Additional clarifications requested by our team:
- Exactly which AWS regions host customer data (data plane + backups) for EU-hosted accounts?
- Does the control plane (account metadata, billing events, logs) ever leave the EU?
- Do any subprocessors process or store customer content outside the EU?
- Are logs or audit trails containing user content or PII accessible outside the EU?

We have a vendor risk review deadline on Mon Aug 17; if you can share the SOC2 redaction and a draft bridge letter (or confirm a timeline for signature) that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Oliver
Vendor Risk (Third-Party Assessment)
NordicBank ASA

Hi Oliver (and Logan),

Thanks — Im Priya from Redwood Security. Below are direct answers and what we can provide immediately.

What we can provide now:
- Redacted SOC 2 Type II report for audit period 2025-10-01 to 2026-03-31 (PDF) — attached (redacted to remove customer-identifying details).
- Draft bridge letter (we can sign and return) — attached as DOCX; we typically agree to an explicit residency commitment for the audit window described in the letter.
- Current subprocessors list (CSV) and a simple dataflow diagram for EU hosting — attached.
- Standard DPA, SCCs (we use EU Standard Contractual Clauses) and applicability notes — we can push these via Drive link or DocuSign.

Technical clarifications (short):
- Data plane: customer content and model-serving artifacts for EU-hosted accounts reside in AWS eu-west-1 (Ireland) or eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) depending on region selection. Backups are retained in the same region by default.
- Control plane: for EU tenant accounts created since 2026-06, the control plane (account metadata and routing) is also hosted in eu-west-1. For older accounts, control plane services may be in an EU region or a restricted EU control plane; we can provision EU-only control plane where required as part of onboarding.
- Logs / audit trails: application logs that may contain identifiers are retained in EU regions for EU-hosted accounts. Where logs contain PII, access controls and retention settings prevent export outside the EU.
- Subprocessors: primary subprocessors that may process metadata or logs include AWS (eu regions), Cloudflare (EU edge), Datadog (EU data residency option available), and Sumo Logic (EU cluster). The attached CSV lists current subprocessors and processing jurisdictions.

Bridge letter scope and signing: we can sign a bridge letter that commits to: (a) retaining customer content in the EU data plane for the audit window; (b) not exporting customer content outside the EU except as required by law; and (c) providing the redacted SOC2 report and subprocessor list as evidence. We ask for minor redline allowances around legal-force wording (standard).

Next steps we propose:
1) I will upload the redacted SOC2 PDF, bridge-letter draft, and subprocessors CSV to the Drive link and attach copies here.
2) Logan will coordinate DocuSign if you want an executed copy; we can typically sign and return a bridge letter within 3 business days of agreement to standard text.
3) If you need a faster SLA, tell us and we will escalate to Legal.

Ive attached: SOC2-2025-10-01_2026-03-31-redacted.pdf, Bridge-Letter-Template-Redwood.docx, Subprocessors-2026-07.csv, Dataflow-EU-hosting.svg.

If you have specific redlines to the draft, please highlight them and well review same-day when possible.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com
